title: My Family Family members
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Protection is taught as body safety with a trusted adult named. Never ask a child to tell the class about abuse; follow the school safeguarding policy if a child discloses. Childline Kenya is 116.

skills.key_step: The child sorts family members into nuclear (parents and children) and extended (grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins) and says that Ephesians 6:1-3 asks children to honour parents, with the promise that it will go well with them.

floor.prerequisite: Can name the people at home.
floor.question: Name two people in your family.

representations: a family tree with two rings: nuclear inside, extended outside
name cards to place on the tree
steps: Put parents and children in the inner ring.
Put grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins in the outer ring.
Say the promise: that it may go well with you.
contexts: a family visit to grandparents at Christmas
a cousin who comes for the school holidays

board.do: Draw two rings and write "nuclear" in the inner ring.
Wait for the child to place her in the extended family.
Write Ephesians 6:2: honour your father and mother.

misconceptions.ask: Who belongs to the extended family?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a small circle for the home and a bigger circle around it for relatives.

listen_for: Only those who live in my house
misconceptions.repair: Ask the child to name a relative who lives far away and how they keep in touch.

listen_for: Only when they give me what I want
misconceptions.ask: When should a child honour his parents, according to Ephesians 6:1-3?
misconceptions.repair: Read Ephesians 6:1-3 and note the word "right" and the promise at the end.

listen_for: Yes, I must obey every adult
misconceptions.ask: An adult relative tells you to steal from a shop. Does honouring your family mean you must do it?
misconceptions.repair: Ephesians 6:1 says obey parents "in the Lord": in what is right. Practise saying no politely to a wrong request.

checks.question: Is an aunt in the nuclear or the extended family?
What promise comes with honouring parents in Ephesians 6:3?
checks.answer: That it may go well with you and you may live long

skills.key_step: The child says NO, goes away and tells a trusted adult if touched wrongly; knows it is never the child's fault, that a secret about touching must be told, and that people a child knows can also do wrong.

floor.prerequisite: Can name people he or she trusts.
floor.question: Name one adult at school you can tell when something is wrong.

representations: the three steps: say NO, go away, tell
a hand with five trusted adults, one on each finger
steps: Say NO in a strong voice.
Go away to a safe place.
Tell a trusted adult at once.
contexts: a phone call from someone the child knows

board.do: Write the three steps: NO, GO, TELL.

board.say: Someone says "keep it a secret". What do you do?

board.do: Wait for the child to say tell a trusted adult.
Write the names of the child's five trusted adults on a hand.

listen_for: Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble
misconceptions.ask: An adult touches you in a way that feels wrong and says "keep it a secret". What should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Say clearly: a secret about touching is never to be kept. Practise telling a teacher or parent.

misconceptions.ask: Who might touch a child in a wrong way?
misconceptions.repair: Teach the rule: private parts are private, whoever asks.

listen_for: The child's fault, so she should say nothing
misconceptions.ask: A child was touched wrongly. Whose fault is it?
misconceptions.repair: Say it slowly: it is never your fault. Name the adults who will believe and help.

misconceptions.ask: A person touched you wrongly once and said sorry. Should you still tell a trusted adult?
misconceptions.repair: Repeat the rule with no exceptions: say no, go away, tell. Name three trusted adults the child could tell.

checks.question: Whose fault is it if a child is touched wrongly?
An adult asks you to keep a touching secret. What do you do?
checks.answer: Say no, go away and tell a trusted adult
